Some of my thoughts on this, not that anyone will ever read this: AI may not "take" your job but employers can still decide you're not needed. AI guided hiring is decimating people looking for jobs--they have to figure out the keywords/algorithm and when they do applications flood in. There's little human input looking at applications now and seeing potential. The barrier to entry keeps getting higher; Master's degrees are required to stand out, and a longer longer list of skills......until you hit 40 and then you're too old. Jobs are becoming shorter term and more unstable, almost at the point in some professions becoming a gig economy, jobs last for a project. Costs for everything are going through the roof, young graduates today face crippling student loans, rent sometimes 50% of their income, and ever more expensive food and utilities.
